quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a guarantee that another driver sees you?

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that another driver sees you. Always assume that any vehicle near your path could enter it.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your bike needs more space to stop. You need more distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic. You need less distance when you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does it mean when the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, as shown in the image?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Ride in a single-file line.
The group will exit soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, it tells the group to form a single-file line.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Go faster.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: How can you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left part of your lane.
Ride in the right part of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Uses some rear braking when you apply the front brake.
Uses some front braking when you apply the rear brake.
Brakes both wheels equally no matter which brake you use.
Remembers how hard you usually brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Uses some front braking when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system automatically applies some front braking when you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual to learn more about your bike's braking system.

questions.question: What is true about the center of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best place for a motorcycle.
It has oil and grease, but is usually safe to ride on.
It has oil and grease, and is never safe to ride on.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has oil and grease, but is usually safe to ride on.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. Avoid large buildups of oil at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: The left side
The center
The right side
It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to cut back in too soon.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grabs again, then brake again.
Release the brake and only use the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. When is this strip safe?

options.text: Never for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless it is raining.
Always avoid it because other parts of the lane are cleaner.
It improves grip for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually provides enough grip for safe riding. The strip is narrow, so you can often stay in the center of the lane and still avoid it.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do them separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When a driver is tailgating you, what is a poor choice?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Let the other driver pass.
Stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If safe, change lanes to let them go ahead. Speeding up only makes it more dangerous because they will tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: During the day, how should you use your headlight?

options.text: Do not use it.
Use the high beam setting.
Use the low beam setting.
Switch between high beam and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the high beam setting.
questions.explanation: Using high beam headlights during the day helps other drivers see you. Use your high beam anytime you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what is the safest approach?

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.
Approach at a 45-degree angle.
Approach at a 90-degree angle.
Go at a high speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: It is safest to go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to approach tracks at a right angle is dangerous because it may send you into another lane.

questions.question: Your lane position should help with all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Avoid surface hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid blind spots, surface hazards, and prevents other drivers from sharing your lane. Your lane position should give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If you take a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Minimize rest breaks.
Use caffeine if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to avoid getting cold during the ride.
Ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to avoid getting cold during the ride.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Limit riding to no more than six hours per day. Take rest breaks at least every two hours. Avoid caffeine and other stimulants, as extreme fatigue occurs when they wear off.

questions.question: How many motorcycle-car crashes are caused by the car driver not yielding right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: Over half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel distances based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan route length based on the least experienced rider's ability. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: When it is raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery when rain starts. Oil from cars has not yet washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: What happens when you brake in a curve?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be careful. Your tires use some grip to make the turn while leaning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: If your front wheel begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride through the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately, then apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.
